svg.title: Invoice retrieval — detailed process
svg.desc: Five actions: receive invoice, view invoice list, select and open invoice, download file, and review and take action. Invoices are received automatically. Users can view saved invoices after access and safety checks, even if ERP delivery is not complete. If the original is not saved, choose a permitted public source or recipient-side private connection and obtain the original. An authorised faithful copy preserves view/download access and public-file evidence while original retrieval is pending. It does not complete ERP intake. No source, denied access and failed retrieval keep original recovery open. Check the recipient account and receiving connection; the customer restores access and the receiving provider checks delivery. Ask the sender for the existing original or destination evidence only if delivery is unresolved. R returns a retrieved file to source and role checks before delivery; its relationship to any saved copy must be proved. From the opened invoice, users can download a file or review and take action. Download is optional. Buyer actions when only a copy is available remain an open decision in SPEC026. The ERP uses Query e-invoices and Retrieve e-invoice for lists, details and file links. The file source sends the selected file through its downloadUrl. Pale green shows customer actions and ERP steps. Pale purple shows getting, checking and processing invoice files. White or light grey shows notes and what is needed before starting. Colours do not show whether a function is ready or built. E marks a problem or pending result. Matching S markers link checked saved files to the invoice list.

g.text: Customer asks sender to confirm the destination
or make the existing original available through the agreed channel.
Missing access alone does not require cancellation or correction.
Invoices are received automatically. Users can view saved invoices after access and safety checks, even if ERP delivery is not complete.
Invoices are collected even when the customer is not signed in.
BEFORE YOU START · Reuse the selected business’s platform setup.
Check receiving-account activation, current connection and permission.
A faithful copy does not prove that receiving access is ready.

S continues at the list request
Choose one invoice from the list.
Or review the invoice. No download needed.
Get file choices and links if needed.
Show the result and any unfinished work.
Check permission. Check that the action is available.

Show whether the list is empty,
Opening does not download or accept the
A derived file is made from the invoice.
Faithful copy: a labelled UBL copy
even while ERP delivery is pending.
ERP receipt does not mean buyer acceptance.
Buyer actions with only a copy available:
Retrieve e-invoice returns file details and links. The file source sends the file when the ERP uses the selected downloadUrl.

Solid: usual flow. Dashed: conditional work or exceptions. E: shared problem result. S: checked saved files for viewing. R: returned file for intake checks. Prove its relationship to any saved copy before ERP delivery.

E · Show the problem or pending result, the reason, the next action and who must act. Keep successful results. Retry only the failed or pending step. If the result is unknown, check what happened before trying again.
The lanes show proposed responsibilities. Implementation support still needs to be confirmed. Shared checks use each country’s rules. The ERP shows file labels and controls its own workflow.
Get, check and process invoice files
Colours group activities. They do not show whether a function is ready or built.
Original unavailable: check account and connection.
Customer completes missing setup or restores access.
Receiving provider checks availability and delivery.
ERP intake pending; safe copy access can continue.
R: save file; check role and matching.
Copy or unclear role: E; review first.
After access is restored, retry the confirmed source.
A returned original follows R; repeat checks and match any saved copy.
Keep invoice information visible while the original is unavailable.

Preserve public-file evidence for later comparison and matching.
The copy does not complete original recovery or ERP intake.
